glicetracker.github.io Yes, it's bad. Very bad. Note the 2014 spike. That's the last time the Ice Caves on the Wisconsin shore were open for any length of time (and it was the first time in years they had been).
💯 I'm the same way, and I think 2014 was the tipping point. That was the last year of Lake Superior ice caves.
Yep this is a classic old school winter. Maybe the Lake Superior Ice Caves might even form.

It's been 10 years since the last time the Lake Superior ice caves formed and were open. But if the cold weather continues I can see them forming this winter. This corner of Lake Michigan has cooled rapidly the last month.

Good evening! On lake Superior every winter, there are spots water runoffs freezing and create ice caves. I've walked across parts of the lake to reach them. It's a bit scary, but an amazing experience. Here is a photo from the outside of the caves.
I'm hoping the Lake Superior ice caves form in the Bayfield, WI area. 2015 was the last time the were available. www.nps.gov/apis/mainlan...

If you’re considering visiting the ice caves on the shores of Lake Superior in WI, don’t do an open water tour or use this business; it’s just too dangerous. This FB warning came from a friend who is a local cop, and the comment thread is full of folks blocked by the business for posting warnings 😳
Lake Michigan’s Ice-water Canyons are no less treacherous than those of Lake Superior!

It's been 4-5 years since we have had big snow winters here in the south central U.P. But I always go back to when the Lake Superior ice caves are able to be traversed, and 2014 was the last winter they were available.
Definitely! We need to push this record up, it's been a while. And it would be nice if we had Lake Superior ice caves to explore again. They haven't formed since 2014.

The northern lights seen through the mouth of an ice cave on the south shore of Lake Superior in WI. An ice cave, unlike glacial caves, are any natural bedrock cave that contains significant amounts of perennial, year-round ice, acting as “underground iceboxes”.

The little ice caves along Lake Superior are a breathtaking winter wonder—sculpted by wind, waves, and freezing temperatures. These frozen formations create a magical landscape that feels straight out of a winter fairy tale. 📸 Captured beautifully by 906 Images
Not like it used to, The Lake Superior ice caves used to form nearly every winter 50 years ago. They were last accessible to the public in 2015. For a quick nine-day window of access
It would take a polar vortex year like 2014 (last time the Lake Superior caves were open) to make it work.
